verdict.root_cause: Checkout's PlaceOrder failures come from the cart service being unreachable at the network/discovery layer, not from anything inside checkout. In every failing trace the deepest erroring span is checkout's own CartService/GetCart client span, terminating in under a millisecond with gRPC UNAVAILABLE and a name-resolver result of zero addresses; all other checkout downstream edges are clean and frontend/frontend-proxy/load-generator merely inherit the error status [tr_6135b12a5275]. Frontend's logs corroborate independently: repeated code-14 transport failures against one address on cart's port 7070, shifting from connection-refused (~23:08) to host-unreachable with the last-error timestamp pinned at 23:33:30.810, plus an explicit cart RPC line whose resolver returned no endpoints [tr_c4267ae5ad55]. Zero resolvable addresses plus host-unreachable to a previously working container IP is cart being severed from the container network, not cart being slow or erroring — no cart-side spans appear in any failing trace. No change sits near onset: checkout's record is empty [tr_985a7c9a2656] and frontend's CART_ADDR edits were reverted ~21h earlier [tr_85dcbca90c10].
verdict.reasoning: Two independent callers converge on the same dependency and mechanism. Traces put the deepest error on checkout's client-side GetCart span with a zero-address resolution failure completing sub-millisecond, excluding timeouts, cart-side application errors, and any fault at the frontend/proxy tier [tr_6135b12a5275]. Frontend logs name cart explicitly and show connection-establishment failures evolving to host-unreachable, still ongoing at the window edge [tr_c4267ae5ad55]. Instant failure rather than hanging distinguishes this from process_freeze, where the socket would still accept. The CART_ADDR override pointed at port 7071 and was reverted ~21h before onset, while observed failures target 7070, so bad_config is not the live mechanism [tr_85dcbca90c10]. Checkout's own log silence [tr_931b8f67cf05] is a logging gap, not a signal — checkout still emits spans.
open_questions: No dispatch touched cart: its logs, metrics, change history and container/network state are entirely unexamined, so the partition is inferred only from callers' symptoms.
Frontend logs show the same endpoint already refusing connections at ~23:08, ~25 minutes before onset — whether that is the same fault or a precursor is unsettled.
Why successful GetCart calls interleave with failures (intermittent resolvability vs. partial endpoint withdrawal) is unexplained.

alternatives.root_cause: Cart's process is stopped or gone while its service record lingers, so callers fail on connect rather than on application errors.
alternatives.why_not: A frozen process keeps its socket accepting and callers hang to deadline; here callers fail in under a millisecond with zero resolved addresses and host-unreachable, which is a network/discovery removal, not a stalled process.

alternatives.root_cause: A stale or wrong cart address/port in the service-discovery or caller configuration directs checkout and frontend at an endpoint that does not serve cart.
alternatives.why_not: The only recorded config edits (CART_ADDR=cart:7071) were reverted ~21.1h before onset and the live failures target the default port 7070, and checkout has no recorded change at all [tr_985a7c9a2656].

proposal.expected_effect: No action proposed, so no effect is expected. The mechanism the evidence supports — cart severed from the container network, seen as zero resolver addresses and host-unreachable to a previously working container IP on cart:7070 [tr_6135b12a5275][tr_c4267ae5ad55] — is addressed by reconnect_service, which this executor cannot perform. The correct next step is not an action but a dispatch against cart itself (its logs, metrics, change history and container/network attachment), which would confirm or refute the partition before anything is changed.
proposal.if_wrong: Abstention is wrong if cart's unexamined record turns out to contain a deploy or config change inside the incident window — that would make rollback_image or revert_config legal on cart and preferable to waiting. It is also wrong if the partition is actually cart's process having died and failed to re-register, in which case restart_service on cart would restore it; but nothing here attests to cart process state, because no dispatch touched cart. Either reading is settled by a change_history and logs/metrics query scoped to cart, not by acting now.
proposal.risk: The risk being avoided: restart_service on cart is the only tempting available action, and its precondition — evidence pointing at process state — is not met. Recreating cart's container would discard its in-process cart cache and drop every in-flight GetCart, and if the fault is a network-layer detachment the recreate may land the container on the same broken attachment, producing an outage with no recovery and destroyed state (restart_service is marked irreversible). A restart would also destroy the evidence needed to distinguish the ~23:08 connection-refused precursor from the 23:33:30 host-unreachable onset [tr_c4267ae5ad55], and would not explain why successful GetCall calls interleave with failures. rollback_image and revert_config fail their preconditions outright: no change is recorded for checkout at all [tr_985a7c9a2656], and frontend's only changes are CART_ADDR edits already reverted ~21h before onset [tr_85dcbca90c10], so there is no in-window change to roll back or revert on any examined service.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody, since nothing changes. For contrast, the action declined — restart_service on cart — would be seen by checkout (PlaceOrder's GetCart and EmptyCart edges) and by frontend's cart RPC path, and through them by frontend-proxy and load-generator, which already inherit cart's error status [tr_6135b12a5275]. Those four services stay in their current partially-failing state while cart is investigated.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Simultaneous critical alerts across checkout, frontend, proxy and load-generator indicate a user-facing outage, not a quiet system. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the shared cause is not inferable from the alerts alone.
